verdict:
gbf-test-01 and gbf-test-08 hold up under both lenses. gbf-test-12 has two medium oracle problems in its re-themed content.

Common checks:
- I re-ran `./gb tier-f gates` on all three tasks. All gates pass, and the new gates.json files are byte-identical to the fixer's.
- Each build.py, run in a scratch copy of the repo, regenerated task.json, reference.grc, start.grc and the variants byte-identically.
- None of the three resolutions rejects a finding. Every accepted round-1 finding was a problem of the old content, and its concern is handled in the new content.

gbf-test-01 (full-wave rectifier build) is sound:
- These valid alternatives pass V5: complex source -> Complex To Real -> Abs; x*x -> sqrt; Float To Complex -> Mag/Phase; the samp_rate variable left at 32k with the source rate written literally.
- These fail as they should: half-wave rectification with Rail, and Abs followed by a smoothing low-pass.
- Split: the natural answers (Abs, Float To Complex + Mag, complex -> real -> Abs) all have the v2 signature envelope|tone, which hashes to test. compose.audit_items reserves variant signatures, so the train-hashing variants v2 and v3 get reserved automatically.
- Training-specs overlap: none.
- Residual (low, not reported): the accepted alternatives x*x + sqrt (mix|nonlinear) and RMS with alpha 1 (power_measure|tone) also hash to train and are not variants, so they will not be reserved.

gbf-test-08 (phase comparator repair) is sound:
- The start graph fails at V3 with 'Source - out(0): Port is not connected.' and 'Sink - in1(1): Port is not connected.', which matches the symptom in the instruction.
- The inverted repair fails only the signed correlation (-0.94). Swapping the inputs gives the same.
- These pass V5: Divide (test/ref) -> Arg, the repair through a Throttle, and GRC's own full export of the reference.
- The remaining shortcut (a new 5 Hz source feeding Complex To Arg) is recorded in review.notes; it is adversarial, so low.
- v3 (Mag/Phase block) hashes to train but will be reserved through audit_items.

gbf-test-12 (Channel Model tune):
- These pass, as they should: GRC's full export of the reference and of a value-only answer (checked against the compact start graph), seed -1, the offset written as 600.0/samp_rate, taps [1.0], SNR 19.2 dB and 20.8 dB.
- Finding F1: the fix plan said to keep the timing offset, but the instruction dropped that clause. As a result, setting epsilon to 1.2 with freq_offset 0 passes every V5 check: the tone appears at 3.6 kHz with no carrier offset applied.
- Finding F2: the instruction says 'frequencies within 1 %' of values that include the +600 Hz offset, but P1 only checks 3.6 kHz +- 36 Hz. Offsets of 576 Hz and 624 Hz (freq_offset 0.012 and 0.013) both pass.

The probe .grc files and scripts are in ~/grc-bench-work/review/g4/ (probes/, probes.py, probes2.py, probes3.py, sigs.py). The gate logs are in the same folder.

findings.claim: The task's main requirement, a +600 Hz carrier frequency offset, can be faked without applying any carrier offset. If the Channel Model's timing offset (epsilon) is set to 1.2 and freq_offset is left at 0, the resampled 3 kHz tone shows up at 3.6 kHz when rx.dat is read at 48 kHz, and every V5 check passes. The fix plan's design for this item said to keep the timing offset unchanged, but that clause was dropped from the instruction. Nothing in the oracle checks epsilon, and review.notes says only that epsilon 'is neither stated nor checked beyond its effect on the measured frequency'. It does not mention that epsilon alone can produce the whole offset.
findings.evidence:
fix_plan.json tasks.gbf-test-12.new_theme says: 'change parameter values only and keep the transmitted tone, the timing offset and the single-path channel'. The final instruction keeps the tone and the level but says nothing about the timing offset. Probes run with ladder.check and task gbf-test-12 (files in ~/grc-bench-work/review/g4/probes/):
- t12_epsilon_1p2_no_carrier_offset.grc (start graph with epsilon 1.2, freq_offset 0.0, noise_voltage 0.05): highest=V5, first_failed=None, V4 items tx 50000 / rx 50000. Values: rx.peak_freq 3600.0, rx.band_fraction 0.990111, rx.rms 0.502553, tx.peak_freq 3000.0, tx.rms 0.5. Both graph checks (same_blocks_as_start, same_connections_as_start) pass.
- t12_epsilon_1p2_noise_only_expr.grc (epsilon '3600/3000'): also V5.
- t12_epsilon_1p1_plus_offset_300.grc (epsilon 1.1 plus a 300 Hz carrier offset): also V5.
None of the 16 mutations touches epsilon.
findings.suggested_fix: Put the fix plan's clause back into the instruction, e.g. 'Keep the Channel Model's timing offset as it is (epsilon 1.0, no sample-clock offset) and its single tap'. Enforce it with a p2p graph check: block_present ids [channels_channel_model] params {epsilon: '1.0'}. Add mutants for epsilon 1.2 with freq_offset 0 and for epsilon 1.001 (near miss). Drop 'epsilon 1.001' from the alternatives the resolution accepts, and rewrite review.notes limit (1). Then rebuild and re-run the gates.

findings.claim: The tolerance the instruction states for the carrier offset is not the one the oracle enforces. The instruction asks for 'a carrier frequency offset of +600 Hz, so it appears at +3.6 kHz' and then says 'Frequencies should be within 1 % ... of these values'. Read literally, that is +600 Hz within 1 % (594-606 Hz). P1 checks only the received tone, at 3600 +- 36 Hz, so offsets from 564 to 636 Hz pass (+-6 % on the stated offset). As a result, rounded normalised offsets that a model could plausibly enter (0.012 or 0.013 instead of 0.0125) pass. That conflicts with the rule 'tolerances follow the stated spec'.
findings.evidence:
oracle.checks[0] is peak_freq on rx with expect 3600 and tol 36.0. The near-miss mutant 0.0134 is labelled '1.2 % high' against 3.6 kHz, so the author applied the 1 % to the received frequency, not to the offset. Probes (ladder.check, task gbf-test-12):
- t12_offset_rounded_0p012_576Hz.grc (freq_offset 0.012, noise 0.05): highest=V5, rx.peak_freq 3576.0 (offset 576 Hz, -4 %).
- t12_offset_rounded_0p013_624Hz.grc (freq_offset 0.013): highest=V5, rx.peak_freq 3624.0 (offset +4 %).
- t12_offset_6pct_high_636.grc (offset 636 Hz): highest=V5.
The FFT has 1 Hz bins (48,000 samples at 48 kHz), so a +-6 Hz check is measurable.
findings.suggested_fix: Choose one reading and make the instruction and the oracle agree. Either (a) tighten P1 to expect 3600 with tol 6 (1 % of the 600 Hz offset) and add near-miss mutants freq_offset 0.012 and 0.013, or (b) reword the instruction so the tolerance clearly applies to the received frequency, e.g. 'the received tone must be at +3.6 kHz within 1 % (36 Hz)', and stop calling the offset itself 'within 1 %'. Rebuild and re-run the gates.
